Mr. Lutfor Rahman Mondal, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record, ------ for the petitioner.

full_judgment:
M. M. Ruhul Amin, J: This Criminal petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 15.5.2003 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Misc. Case No. 2103 of 1995 filed against the judgment and order dated 26.6.1995 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, 7th Court, Dhaka in Criminal Revision No. 147 of 1995 modifying the judgment and order dated 19.4.1995 passed by the Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka in Petition Case No. 892a1/1991 taking cognizance under section 408/468/471 of the Penal Code. 

 2. The complainant's representative filed the complaint case No. 892a1/1991 before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka on 14.8.1991 on behalf of the two registered companies. 

 3. Short facts of the case are that the accused petitioners are inter related to one another and while they were in service in the aforesaid companies, they collusively by forging cheques, vouchers and others papers and by committing criminal breach of trust with the object of cheating the aforesaid companies misappropriated an amount of Taka-1, 25,84,245/- at different times during the period from 1987 Ad to 1990 Ad. The accused persons by mis-appropriating monies acquired huge movable and immovable properties; that for the purpose of showing forgery, cheating and criminal breach of trust the complainant produced 3 audit reports to cover the offences under sections' 468/420/408/109 of the Penal Code. 

 6. The accused petitioner No. 1 on 13.8.1992 filed Title Suit No. 171 of 1992 against the aforesaid companies for declaring certain documents which are the basis and foundation of the complainant's case, as forged and illegal along with a claim for total damages of Taka 1,27,35,506/-. 

 7. The accused petitioners filed Criminal Revision No. 17 of 1992 before the Sessions Judge Dhaka under section 435/438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which was rejected on 19.10.1992, and the accused petitioners filed an application before the learned Magistrate under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking stay of the Criminal case because of filing the Title Suit No. 171 of 1992 and that application was rejected on 14.11.1992. Against that order the accused petitioners filed Criminal Revision No. 1890 of 1992 before the High Court Division, and the Rule was made absolute on 9.3.1994 with the direction to the court below to dispose of the Title Suit within six months. Against that judgment and order of the High Court Division the complainant filed Appeal before the Appellate Division being Appeal No. 6 of 1994. 

 8. The complainant filed Money Suit No. 7 of 1994 on 20.1.1994 for realization of the alleged misappropriated monies against the accused persons. The accused petitioners accordingly filed an application for analogous hearing of the aforesaid Title Suit No. 171 of 1992 and Money Suit No. 7 of 1994 and the application was allowed. The complainant at the time of filing the money suit produced all the alleged forged vouchers, receipts and other documents in original before the Court for the purpose of proving the alleged forgery, fabrication of accounts and misappropriation of money. The Appeal No. 6 of 1994 was allowed with direction to the Magistrate to dispose of the Criminal case expeditiously. The accused persons on 8.10.1994 filed an application under section 227(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the application was rejected. The accused petitioners then filed Criminal Revision No. 380 of 1994 before the Sessions Judge, Dhaka who disposed of the application on 25.10.1994 with the direction to the learned Magistrate to the effect that under section 227(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure the charge can be amended at any time before passing judgment. The accused persons filed an appellation for transfer of the case before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka and the application was not disposed of. The accused persons again filed an application to dispose of the petition dated 8.11.1994 filed before the Metropolitan Magistrate which was rejected on 11.1.1995. The accused persons filed Criminal Revision No. 29 of 1995 before the Sessions Judge, Dhaka on 1.2.1995 for setting aside the order dated 14.8.1991 taking cognizance, the order dated 1.10.1991 framing charge and the order dated 11.1.1995 as aforesaid. At the time of admission of the revisional application the learned Sessions Judge, admitted the application only against the order dated 11.1.1995 with observation that the order dated 14.8.1991 and 1.10.1991 were time barred and the case was heard by the Additional Sessions Judge, 7th Court, Dhaka and the case was allowed on 1.3.1995 with observation that "thus it appears that the alleged charges under section 408 and 420 of the Penal Code framed for a period exceeding twelve months are clearly hit by section 239C Cr.P.C. Therefore it is needless to say that the learned Magistrate framed the alleged charges illegally in gross violation of the provisions laid down in section 239C Cr.P.C. Such illegalities are not curable under section 537 of Cr.P.C." Accordingly on 1.4.1995 a date was fixed for framing charge and on that date the accused petitioners filed an application under section 241A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for discharging the accused persons and on 19.4.1995 that application was rejected and the charges were framed on 19.4.1995 under sections 408/468/471 of the Penal Code. The accused persons then filed Criminal Revision No. 147 of 1995 and the application was admitted and disposed of on 26.6.1995 allowing the application partly. Against the judgment and order an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure was filed which was rejected by a Division Bench of the High Court Division on 15.4.2003. 

 11. We have perused the judgment of the High Court Division and also other related papers. It appears that the learned Additional Sessions Judge passed judgment and order dated 26.9.95 in Criminal Revision No. 147 of 1995 modifying the judgment and order dated 19.4.95 passed by the Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka in Petition Case No. 892a1/91 and directed the Magistrate to frame charge under section 468/471 of the Penal Code and to dispose of the case as expeditiously as possible. The High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order discharged the Rule affirming the judgment and order passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Dhaka. It may be stated here that this case has a chequred history as there were series of litigations both civil and criminal between the parties as already stated. The High Court Division after assigning good reasons found that there is no irregularity or illegality in the impugned order and the provisions of section 195(1) Cr.P.C. are not attracted in the case. It is clear that the High Court Division on proper assessment and on consideration of the legal position arrived at a correct decision. 

 12. Mr. Rafiq-ul-Huq the learned Senior Advocate entering the caveat for the respondent no. 1 submits that criminal case should be disposed of as quickly as possible so that justice may be available to the parties without unnecessary delay. In support of his contention the learned Counsel has placed before us the photocopy of the judgment in Criminal Appeal No. 6 of 1994 of this Division disposed of on 22nd August, 1994.
